shortlist.scout_ahead_today: scout.py cmd_question stores text only; cmd_answer stores the answer. shortlist.mechanic: Builder check: once the written design exists, a fresh agent that cannot talk to the author reads only the document and reports just the questions where a wrong guess would matter, ranked, or 'nothing important left'. The author then sorts them into three piles: already answered (fix the doc), minor (settle it and mark it as your call), theirs (one message, most important first). There is one round only.

shortlist.quote: You've been handed a design document and asked to put together a plan to build what it describes. You will not be able to talk to the person who wrote it. ... Report only the questions you'd still need answered before you could plan this well: places where you'd have to guess and a wrong guess would matter.
shortlist.scout_ahead_today: plugins/scout/skills/handoff/SKILL.md step 3: 'Read it back once as the downstream reader would'. This is a self-read by the same session that wrote the record. scripts/scout.py cover_gaps() only checks that ids, directions, branches and parked questions appear in the text. It cannot tell whether a reader could act on them.
shortlist.proposed_change: scout.py: new subcommand `coldread [--usd 0.5] [--model opus]`. It spawns `claude -p --model opus --max-budget-usd <usd> --allowedTools Read --no-session-persistence` and builds the command with a helper shared with _run_arm (DRY). The prompt adapts the builder-check text: 'you will turn this into a spec; you cannot talk to whoever ran the scout; read scouting/<slug>/handoff.md; report only questions where a wrong guess changes the plan, ranked; else nothing important left'. The output is written to scouting/<slug>/coldread.md, the cost is added to spent.usd, and the run is logged as an entry. handoff/SKILL.md step 3 becomes: run coldread, then sort each question. Answered by the record or the code: fix it with decide/answer/note and regenerate. Minor: settle it and record it as the scout's call (see the next candidate). Theirs: `question` or `decide --by open --ask` so it lands in Open questions. Only one round runs. The final message lists the 'theirs' pile, most important first.
